title: Neighbourhood Quality Scoring

blueprintSignals.name: Walk time to amenities
blueprintSignals.definition: routing time on the pedestrian network to the nearest grocery, school, park and transit stop
blueprintSignals.asOfRule: Use the current map snapshot for training labels and do not mix in later openings

blueprintSignals.name: Street imagery greenery
blueprintSignals.definition: share of pixels classed as tree canopy in street-level images, averaged over each cell
blueprintSignals.asOfRule: Images are seasonal, so normalise by capture month and never compare winter to summer

blueprintSignals.name: Business openings
blueprintSignals.definition: net new registered businesses in the cell over 24 months, divided by existing businesses
blueprintSignals.asOfRule: Registrations lag opening, so count by registration date and exclude the scored quarter

blueprintSignals.name: Noise exposure
blueprintSignals.definition: modelled decibel level from road, rail and flight-path data at the cell centroid
blueprintSignals.asOfRule: The model assumes typical traffic, so re-run it after a major route change

engineFeatures.meaning: the strongest continuous driver; interacts with x2 and shifts in the last quarter
modifies the effect of x1 and sets the noise level
a smooth non-linear effect that a straight line cannot fit
a categorical segment with its own level and noise

label: For "Neighbourhood Quality Scoring": Score each neighbourhood on walkability, amenities, safety perception, noise and change so buyers and investors can compare areas. Define the label exactly as in milestone M1: what counts as a positive or a correct outcome, and when it becomes known. Design around this trap first: Survey calibration data covers wealthy and responsive areas better than others.
